Valerian.wikitext:
{{AdeptusCustodesPortal}} {{otheruses|USE=Custodian|OTHERUSE=[[Black Templars|Black Templar]]|OTHERPAGE=Valerian (Black Templars)}} {{Character |Portal ={{AdeptusCustodesPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =ValerianAleya.png |Caption =Shield-Captain Valerian and [[Sisters of Silence|Sister]] [[Tanau Aleya]]{{Fn|2}} |Title =The Hero of Lion's Gate |Homeworld =[[Terra]] |Birth = |Active Period =??? - Present |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Custodes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation ='' '' *[[Shield Captain]] of the [[Adeptus Custodes]]
(Former) |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Adeptus Custodes]] ***[[Hykanatoi]] |Notes = }} '''Valerian''' was a [[Adeptus Custodes]] [[Shield-Captain]] within the [[Hykanatoi]]'s Palaiologian Chamber during the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}} He was later named the '''Hero of Lion's Gate''' by [[Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]]{{Fn|3b}} for his efforts during the Crusade's battles on [[Terra]] and [[Vorlese]].{{Fn|3a}} ===Biography=== ====13th Black Crusade==== While taking part in a [[Blood Game]], during the Crusade's fifth year, he was asked by the [[Hetaeron Guard]]'s [[Custodian Tribune|Tribune]], [[Heracleon]], to join their order. This was a great honour for Valerian, as he had long strived to join the Companions, and prepared himself to face the Hetaeron Guard's first trial. It seemed simple enough, as he had to simply enter the chamber of the [[Golden Throne]] that held the [[Emperor]], but after catching a glimpse of the Master of Mankind, Valerian body froze and would not obey him. This caused him to fail the trial and Valerian was left ashamed and embarrassed{{Fn|1b}} as he was returned to his former duties of guarding the [[Imperial Palace]]'s outer walls. He later aided in the Palace's defense as mayhem swept across [[Terra]] in the aftermath of the [[Great Rift]]'s creation.{{Fn|1c}} Valerian was part of the 4,000 Custodes warriors which took part in the [[Second Battle of Terra]] against the forces of [[Khorne]], during which he met the [[Sister of Silence]] [[Tanau Aleya]]. Valerian, Aleya, several Sisters, and a squad of [[Grey Knights]] managed to take down a [[Bloodthirster]] in the battle. As they were about to be overwhelmed, [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris]] led a charge from the [[Lion's Gate]] that swept across the Chaos forces.{{Fn|1d}} Following the assault on Terra, Valerian agreed to join Aleya in a bid to follow her captured [[Black Legion]] [[Warp]] route map to take the fight to Chaos forces. Joined by a mixed force of 40 Sisters of Silence and nine other Custodians, Valerian and Aleya journeyed to [[Vorlese]] aboard the Custodes ship ''[[Chelandion]]''. Once there they found the world [[Battle of Vorlese|under assault]] from the Black Legion which planned to drop a shard of a [[Cadian Pylon]] onto the planets surface to shut down all Warp travel in the area and isolate Terra.{{Fn|1e}} Valerian, Aleya, and their small band teleported aboard the [[Grand Cruiser]] ''[[Heartspite]]'' at the center of the assault, fought their way to the Pylon shard, and in a desperate last stand prevented it from being dropped onto the planet. The entire force was slaughtered in the process save for Valerian, Aleya, and the Custodes [[Ujoma]]. All three were left badly wounded, when [[Roboute Guilliman]]'s fleet later arrived and defeated the Black Legion by seizing the ''Heartspite''. Valerian and the other survivors were then rushed to Terra to receive priority medical care, and all three survived their wounds, though Ujoma was interred inside a [[Contemptor Dreadnought]].{{Fn|3a}} ====Era Indomitus==== {{Spoiler|source=Watchers of the Throne: The Regent's Shadow (Novel)}} After he had recovered, Guilliman asked to meet with Valerian and thanked the Shield-Captain for his heroic efforts. When Valerian learned that Guilliman planned on launching the [[Indomitus Crusade]], he asked to join and fight beside the Lord Commander. Guilliman, though, declined stating that he would defer to Custodes' [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris]]' judgement that Valerian should stay to defend Terra. When the Crusade launched, the Throne World would need to look to its own forces to protect it. He did, however, want to honor Valerian in the tradition of [[Ultramar]], during a ceremony celebrating other worthy participants of the wars on [[Terra]] and [[Vorlese]]. This would make Valerian an important symbol to the population of Terra and while the Shield-Captain's heart told him he should decline, Valerian ultimately accepted Guilliman's request.{{Fn|3a}} The Shield-Captain took part in the ceremony alongside his comrade, the [[Witch Seeker]] [[Aleya]], though, she avoided his attempts to contact her. He did not know it, but Aleya only did so due to not being used to non-members of her Order treating her with comradery, instead of scorn. Valerian did have long to think on this, however, as Guilliman presented him to the crowd watching the ceremony and crowned the Shield-Captain with a laurel wreath taken from Ultramar. Then before the adulating crowds, the [[Lord Commander]] proclaimed Valerian the [[Hero of the Lion's Gate]], an ancient honor used only once before, when [[Terra]] was [[Battle for Terra|invaded]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|3b}} Not all those in the Custodes enthused by Valerian accepting the honor, however, and some now saw him as Guilliman's lackey. The Shield-Captain, though, believed in the [[Lord Commander]]'s vision for the future of the [[Imperium]] and Valerian was willing to become one of the symbols he needed to complete his grand task. Yet not helping matters, was the fact that Guilliman personally requested that Valerian head an investigation into the [[Splintered (Chaos Cult)|Splintered]] [[Cults]] that were wreaking havoc on [[Terra]]. [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris]] agreed and Valerian was given command of a group of Custodes, called the [[Argent Chamber]], to aid him in his quest. Valerian's first act was to order an attack on the [[Heretic]] [[Laxlan Skreto]], who was one of the Cults' many leaders. The Custodes' intelligence stated that Skreto's Cult had laid claim to Terra's '''Gorgantha subsector''' and had repelled the [[23rd Hajada Erthguard]]'s efforts to destroy them. This resistance ended, however, when Valerian led a direct strike at Skreto's stronghold and killed the Splintered's forces defending it, before capturing the Cult leader. Skreto was then interrogated by the Custodes{{Fn|3c}} and through him, they learned of many of the Spintered's other Cult leaders, such as [[Fyger Deflaim]], the [[Lachrymosa]] and the [[Convolute]]. By then, though, the [[Imperial Fists]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]], [[Tor Garadon]] and his [[Space Marine Company|Company]] had arrived to Terra aboard the [[Phalanx]], from the battlefield of [[Cadia]]. With his arrival, Captain-General Trajann Valoris, wished for Terra's population to see the Imperial Fists taking the fight to the Splintered, while the Custodes assumed their traditional role of being in the background. As such, he ordered that Valerian cede the leadership of the investigation to Tor Garadon, which the Shield-Captain reluctantly did. After Valerian shared the information the Heretic Skreto gave to them, Garadon decided to strike at the stronghold of the Splintered Cult leader, known as the Convolute.{{Fn|3d}} With the combined might of the [[Custodes]] and [[Imperial Fists]], the [[Convolute]]'s [[Heretic]] forces were easily killed. But even as his Cult was being torn apart, the furious Convolute unleashed his powers and raved at Valerian, that by attacking him they were only making his rival, the [[Lachrymosa]], stronger. The Convolute was then quickly mortally wounded, but before the Shield-Captain could kill him, the Heretic was blown apart by a [[Minotaurs]] squadron that suddenly appeared.{{Fn|3e}} The squadron was then questioned by Valerian, but they refused to answer any of his questions. Due to negative past encounters between their Chapters, [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Tor Garadon]] ordered the Minotuars to leave immediately. The squadron refused and the two Chapters would have come to blows, had Valerian and his [[Argent Chamber]] not placed themselves between the [[Space Marines]]. The Shield-Captain then forced them both to stand down, and the Minotaurs left without explaining their actions or why they were on Terra. Afterwards, Valerian informed the Custodes of the Minotuars' presence and their enmity with the Imperial Fists. With that duty done, the Shield-Captain was left intrigued by the hatred in which the Convolute spoke of his rival the Lachrymosa. Seeking to hunt her down, Valerian sought the aid of the [[Eye of the Emperor]] [[Kalluin]], to learn more about her. After gathering information through his spy network, however, Kalluin informed Valerian that the Lachyrmosa was the weakest of the remaining Splintered Cult leaders.{{Fn|3f}} Nonetheless, Valerian felt compelled to search for her, as he continued his efforts to destroy the Splintered.{{Fn|3g}} During that time, Valerian was approached by his comrade the [[Sister of Silence]] [[Aleya]], who sought his aid in an investigation she was undertaking. As Custodes had battled the [[Splintered (Chaos Cult)|Splintered]] [[Chaos Cult]]s, the Sisters' [[Somnus Citadel]] stronghold was struck by a failed attempted to destroy it with a bomb-filled lander. Aleya had then tracked down the some of the culprits, but they killed themselves, or were murdered. She, however, found a [[auto-catechism]] device, which led her to believe the [[Imperial Church]] member known as ''Peder''' was behind the attack and asked Valerian if he knew who that was. After pouring through the device, the [[Shield-Captain]] determined that the Peder in the notes, likely referred to the deposed [[Ecclesiarch]] and [[High Lord]] [[Baldo Slyst]], who had been removed from power by [[Guilliman]]. Now that she finally had a target to go after, Aleya asked Valerian to join in her hunt, but he refused due to his orders to strike down the leadership of the Splintered Cults. Before she left, however, the Shield-Captain gave Aleya his [[Misericordia]] to wield against Slyst.{{Fn|3h}} Soon afterwards the Splintered took such heavy losses at the [[Minotaurs]]' hands, that the Cults rallied under the leadership of [[Fyger Deflaim]] for a final stand in the '''Cathedral of the Emperor Deified'''. Valerian and the [[Argent Chamber]] were part of the Imperial forces sent to confront them, but all were surpised when the Minotaurs launched a sudden strike and destroyed the Splintered Cults. Afterwards, it was revealed that the Minotaurs were acting on the behalf{{Fn|3i}} of the [[Hexarchy]] - a group of current and deposed [[High Lords]], that sought to overthrow Guilliman's rule of the Imperium. They broadcasted the Splintered' defeat across Terra, showing that they and not Guilliman would restore order to the Throne World. The Hexarchy then demanded that the High Lords loyal to Guilliman stand down and cede rule of Terra to them.{{Fn|3j}} The [[Hexarchy]] and the Loyalists, led by [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris|Valoris]], then entered a stalemate, as their terms were considered, but this was nearly undone due to a group of [[Sisters of Silence]] led by [[Aleya]]. The former [[Ecclesiarch]] [[Baldo Slyst]] was a member of the Hexarcy and she led her Sisters into the Cathedral, to kill her long sought after target despite being heavily outnumbered. Captain-General Valoris, ordered Valerian, who was nearby, to stop her and he led his [[Argent Chamber]] after Aleya. Using the homing beacon on the [[Misericordia]] he had given her, Valerian was able to catch up to Aleya's group, just as they began to battle a squadron of [[Minotaurs]] that had discovered them. Valerian immediately led his forces to their aid{{Fn|3j}} and both groups succeeded in killing the Minotaurs, though not without suffering losses. The Shield-Captain then attempted to convince Aleya to withdraw, but she refused and instead asked him to join her in attacking Slyst.{{Fn|3k}} Valerian ultimately relented and agreed to aid her and both groups advanced onto Slyst' postion.{{Fn|3l}} It was then, however, that the traitorous [[High Lord]] [[Fadix]] revealed that his loyalty to the Hexarchy's cause had been a ruse from the start. He was the [[Grand Master of Assassins]] and after a signal was given, each of the Hexarchy's members were killed by Fadix's well placed assassins.{{Fn|3m}} Valerian at once realized, that [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris|Valoris]] had used [[Aleya]]'s attack as an excuse to get him into the Cathedral, so that the [[Shield-Captain]] could ensure [[Fadix]]'s survival. Both the [[Sisters of Silence|Sisters]] and [[Custodes]] then raced to Fadix's side and defended him from both the [[Astra Militarum]] [[Regiments]] that had been tricked into aiding the [[Hexarchy]], as well as the [[Minotaurs]] [[Chapter]]. In the confusion that followed the Hexarchy's deaths, the two groups successfully did so and eventually the Astra Militarum and Minotaurs obeyed orders to stand down from the loyalist [[High Lords]].{{Fn|3m}} After the battle, Aleya visited Valerian and informed him she intended to keep the [[Shield-Captain]]'s [[Misericordia]] until she had made a worthy kill with it. When Valerian stated that meant their paths would cross again, Aleya told the Shield-Captain he was likely right before she then departed for [[Luna]].{{Fn|3n}} Valerian later met with Captain-General Valoris, who informed him that not all of the [[Splintered (Chaos Cult)|Splintered]] had been destroyed, as they had originally thought. As most of Splintered' forces were being destroyed in the Cathedral by the Minotaurs, the [[Lachrymosa]]'s Cult had escaped Terra aboard several captured space ships. Valoris then explained to Valerian, that the [[heretic]] [[Convolute]] had been correct about the Lachrymosa's power. The Captain-General now considered the escaped Cult leader to have been the greatest threat amongst the Splintered and he ordered Valerian to hunt her down.{{Fn|3o}} ===Wargear=== Valerian wields the [[Guardian Spear]] ''[[Gnosis (Guardian Spear)|Gnosis]]''.{{Fn|3a}} ===Images=== [[Image:ValerianMini.jpg|thumb|center|160px|Valerian miniature{{Fn|2}}]] ===Sources=== *1: [[Watchers of the Throne: The Emperor's Legion (Novel)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Valerian Chapter 1 **{{Endn|1b}}: Valerian Chapter 3 **{{Endn|1c}}: Valerian Chapter 4 **{{Endn|1d}}: Chapters 13–14 **{{Endn|1e}}: Chapters 25–29 *{{Endn|2}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2019/11/10/black-library-weekender-2019-the-reveals/ Black Library Weekender 2019: The Reveals (posted 10 November 2019)] ''(Last accessed 11/12/2019)'' *3: [[Watchers of the Throne: The Regent's Shadow (Novel)]] **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter 2 - Valerian **{{Endn|3b}}: Chapter 3 - Aleya **{{Endn|3c}}: Chapter 5 - Valerian **{{Endn|3d}}: Chapter 8 - Valerian **{{Endn|3e}}: Chapter 11 - Valerian **{{Endn|3f}}: Chapter 14 - Valerian **{{Endn|3g}}: Chapter 17 - Valerian **{{Endn|3h}}: Chapter 18 - Aleya **{{Endn|3i}}: Chapter 20 - Valerian **{{Endn|3j}}: Chapter 23 - Valerian **{{Endn|3k}}: Chapter 24 - Aleya **{{Endn|3l}}: Chapter 26 - Valerian **{{Endn|3m}}: Chapter 28 - Valerian **{{Endn|3n}}: Chapter 29 - Aleya **{{Endn|3o}}: Chapter 31 - Valerian [[Category:Characters (Adeptus Custodes)]] [[Category:Characters (Black Crusades)]]

Valgard Twice-Slain.wikitext:
{{SpaceWolvesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Space Wolves]] [[Grey Hunter]], who was given command of a strike force to complete a mission for his [[Chapter]]{{Fn|1a}}. However disaster struck, when the [[Strike Cruiser]] they were traveling in emerged from the [[Warp]] near [[Kanak]] and was suddenly attacked by a [[Word Bearers]] [[Murder Class Cruiser]]. Caught off guard by the attack, the Strike Cruiser was destroyed and its wreckage fell upon Kanak, though some of the Space Wolves' strike force managed to survive the crash{{Fn|1b}}. What they found when they emerged was an Imperium world, that had been successfully invaded by a Word Bearers Warband led by the [[Dark Apostle]] [[Oriax (Word Bearers)|Oriax the Persuader]], whose forces began mercilessly hunting the Space Wolves down. Valgard himself was among those who survived the Strike Cruiser's crash and he quickly organized other survivors from the strike force he found and began bringing the fight to the Word Bearers themselves{{Fn|1a}}. Despite being heavily outnumbered, Valgard's force defeated every traitor they faced and soon found Oriax within a [[Xenos]] temple, where the Dark Apostle was conducting a Chaos ritual in front of an obelisk. The ritual would free a [[Slaanesh]] [[Keeper of Secrets]], imprisoned within a [[Tesseract Labyrinth]], who would then grant the Dark Apostle's wish for immortality - something he graciously offered to share with the Space Wolves, if they joined him in the worship of Chaos. The Space Wolves refused though and fought through the Dark Apostle's forces within the temple and defeated Oriax before he could complete the ritual. The energy unleashed by Dark Apostle's ritual though, had awoken the temple's [[Necron]] creators, who soon emerged from their slumber and began attacking both the Space Wolves and Word Bearers.{{Fn|1c}}

Valiance.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
[[Commissar]] '''Valiance ''' was the given name to a [[human]] on the planet [[Kronus]], who styled himself after the [[Imperium]]'s [[Commissar]]s. Before the [[Dark Crusade]], when the [[Tau]] still controlled Kronus, Valiance was a agitator operating in the Orestan industrial cities; who incited the human population to acts of violence toward the Tau's [[Earth Caste|Earth]] and [[Water Caste]] citizens in the cities. During one such riot Valiance would drag an Earth Caste worker onto a makeshift stage and murder him in cold blood. Through these acts of violence, Valiance hoped to overthrow the Tau and return the planet to the Imperium's rule. The Tau's leadership on Kronus, considered Valiance a threat to the [[Greater Good]] and ordered its security teams to be on the lookout for the self-styled Commissar.{{Fn|1}}

By the time the [[Ministorum]] learned of this and sought Valious' finger bone, Lisp had been killed and the relic bone was gone. (Formerly) *[[Ancient]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Realm of Ultramar]] **[[Ultramarines]] ***[[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] ****Gadriel’s Squad ****[[Wardens of Ultramar]] |Notes = }} '''Valorem Gadriel'''{{fn|2e}} is the [[Ancient]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]]'s [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] under the reinstated command of [[Demetrian Titus]]. Before that, he served as a [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] in command of a squad of his own.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}} ===History=== Inducted into the Ultramarines after making a pilgrimage to their fortress of [[Castra Tanagra]] on his home planet of [[Talassar]], Gadriel's unrelenting will quickly caught the attention of [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Sevastus Acheran]] who invited him the illustrious [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]], where he swiftly made the rank of [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]].{{fn|2e}} Gadriel, alongside his squadmate [[Chairon]], were the Ultramarines placed under the command of the newly returned [[Demetrian Titus]] by [[Captain]] [[Sevastus Acheran]].{{Fn|2a}} Gadriel was obedient but distrustful of Titus due to his background as a [[Deathwatch Blackshield]] and seeming connection to [[Project Aurora]] and the [[Inquisition]].{{Fn|2b}} These suspicions come to a head while battling the [[Thousand Sons]] on [[Avarax]] after an [[Astropath]] accuses Titus of being a heretic who plans to kill [[Marneus Calgar]]. Gadriel attempts to kill Titus to save Calgar and stop the [[Chaos]] plot, but thanks to Chairon killing the Astropath it is revealed that the [[Psyker]] had in fact been possessed by the [[Sorcerer]] [[Imurah]].{{Fn|2c}} After witnessing his manipulation with Imurah, Gadriel takes an apologetic tone with Titus, which the Lieutenant dismisses as he says his suspicions were reasonable. Together with Titus and Chairon, the trio are able to defeat Imurah and his allied [[Lord of Change]].{{Fn|2d}} Gadriel later joined Titus' Command squad within the 2nd Company as a [[Ancient|Company Ancient]].{{Fn|4}} ===Images=== GadrielJoytoy.jpg|Gadriel action figure from [[Joytoy]]{{Fn|3}} Gadriel-Ancient-2026.jpg|[[Ancient]] Gadriel miniature (2026){{Fn|4}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/warhammer-40000-space-marine-2-preview/ Digital Trends: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Preview (Posted on 23/08/2023)] (Last accessed on 23/08/2023) *{{Endn|2}}: [[Space Marine 2]] **{{Endn|2a}}: Mission 2, Severance **{{Endn|2b}}: Mission 3, Machinus Divinitus **{{Endn|2c}}: Mission 4, Voidsong **{{Endn|2d}}: Mission 5, Dawn's Descent **{{Endn|2e}}: Datavault Research Centre *{{Endn|3}}: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240924050323/https://www.joytoy.com/products/?&Narrow=4_2%7C615bf6db4dee158ccbbc1ed5aef1ced9 Joytoy] saved page, original link: https://www.joytoy.com/products/?&Narrow=4_2%7C615bf6db4dee158ccbbc1ed5aef1ced9 (last accessed 24/9/2024) *{{Endn|4}}: [https://archive.ph/THOjJ Warhammer Community: World Championships Preview – Captain Titus battles Nekrosor Ammentar for the Five Hundred Worlds of Ultramar] ''(Saved archive page, dated 7 November 2025, last accessed 7 November 2025, original link: https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/fm2tm39s/world-championships-preview-captain-titus-battles-nekrosor-ammentar-for-the-five-hundred-worlds-of-ultramar/)'' [[Category:Characters (Ultramarines)]] [[Category:Characters (Tyrannic Wars)]]

Van Cjester.wikitext:
'''Van Cjester''' was the inventor of the [[Steel Fury Baneblade Company]].  His writing, titled ''Differential Theorem of Dispersed Attrition'', states that while a single allied tank may be equal to a single enemy tank, two tanks are three times as effective, due to the enemy being both outgunned 2:1 and having to destroy two tanks to survive.

His death came when his [[Baneblade]] was crushed by a traitor [[titan]] at the [[Battle of Ununpentia Gorge]], but his life is celebrated by armoured regiments on [[501]], which involves a feast.  He was also made a [[Sanctus Militarus]] three centuries after his death.

Vandius.wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
[[Ancient]] '''Vandius''' is a [[Space Marine]] from the [[Ultramarines]]' [[chapter]] and [[Company Standard Bearer]] for the 2nd Company, attached to [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Cato Sicarius]]'s [[Space Marine Command Squad|Command Squad]], "The Lions of Macragge."{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
===Black Reach===
During the [[Assault on Black Reach]] in 855 [[M41]]{{Fn|1b}}, the 2nd Company was deployed to [[Black Reach]] against [[Waaagh!]] [[Zanzag]], and the Lions fought in the vanguard of the [[Drop Pod]] assault with Sicarius, and in subsequent engagements.{{Fn|2}}.

===Espandor===
During the attack of the [[Bloodborn]] on [[Ultramar]], in 854999.M41{{Fn|1b}}, the 2nd Company was deployed to [[Espandor]]. After some initial skirmishes, Captain Sicarius decided that the best way to bring the campaign to a swift end was to locate and kill the attacking force's commander, the Corsair Queen [[Kaarja Salombar]] {{Fn|3a}}{{Fn|3b}}.

[[Tactical Squad]] [[Scipio Vorolanus|Vorolanus]] located Salombar in the city of [[Corinth (city)|Corinth]], and Sicarius swiftly launched a full assault. The Lions of Macragge spearheaded the charge into the Corsair ranks, Sicarius ferociously set on confronting Salombar in close combat{{Fn|3c}}.

Salombar was a skilled sword-fighter, and lopped off Vandius's standard arm. Sgt. Vorolanus, standing nearby, stopped the [[Space Marine Standards|Company Standard]] from touching the ground, and could see that the loss of his arm pained Vandius less than almost failing in his duty to keep the standard aloft{{Fn|3d}}.

==Trivia==
The Ultramarines [[First Company]]'s third squad of [[Terminator]]s is led by a Sergeant named Vandius{{Fn|4}}. This may be the same individual, but it is unlikely.

Vandoth.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
'''Vandoth the Fallen''' is a giant masked man who is bound in layers of crimson muscle and his exploits on [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]] have made him a figure of legend on the [[hive world]].{{Fn|1}}  

==Biography==
[[file:Vandoth.png|thumb|right|180px|Vandoth the Fallen{{Fn|1}}]]
Stories are told of his ability to crush a man's skull with one hand and turn aside blades with his hardened skin. Most disturbing of all, though, are the tales of Vandoth's unquenchable thirst for blood. It is said that hidden behind his mask are long canine fangs, and after he kills, the gigantic warrior stoops over his prey to drain them dry.{{Fn|1}}

There are conflicting accounts as to where Vandoth originally came from and who (or even what) he is. Some insist the massive warrior was once a [[House Goliath|Goliath]], somehow corrupted in the vat with tainted blood. Others believe he was once one of Lord [[Gerontius Helmawr|Helmawr]]'s personal guards until he was genetically altered into a [[vampire|vampiric]] beast for the ruler of Necromunda's amusement. Then there are the stories that Vandoth is a thing of [[Chaos]], though the savagery that he shows to those corrupted by the [[Dark Gods]] would seem to discount this. All that is known for sure is Vandoth has wandered Necromunda for centuries at least, his face hidden behind a mask and an ancient oversized [[boltgun]] at his side.{{Fn|1}}

Outlaws will sometimes pay for Vandoth's aid with the promise of coin, weapons, or glory, though the giant mostly does as he pleases, aiding others when his interests align with theirs.{{Fn|1}}

Vandt.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Vandt''' was the [[Imperial Commander]] of [[Sirene Primal]], when the secessionist '''Sirene Monarch''' began a rebellion against the [[Imperium]]'s rule of the world.{{Fn|1}}

==History==
[[Sirene Primal]] martial sect warriors joined the rebellion, as they had long chafed under the [[Imperium]], and this greatly aided the '''Monarch'''. As the warriors were highly respected in Sirene's culture, the rest of the population rebelled as well and its inexperienced [[PDF]] did not resist either. This led Vandt to be ousted as Sirene Primal's ruler and he was replaced by the Monarch. It is not known what became of Vandt afterwards, but several [[Astra Militarum]] [[Regiments]] were sent to reclaim the world. During the war's 4th year, the [[Inquisitor]] [[Obodiah Roth]] discovered that the Monarch was a [[Genestealer Cultist]] and the Regiments soon located and killed the corrupted Cult leader. However it was too late, as the Cult had successfully drawn a massive [[Hive Fleet]] to Sirene. Inquisitor Roth then urged the [[Imperial Navy]] fleet above the world to retreat, after evacuating all senior officers and dignitaries from the world. It would do so, before the Hive Fleet [[Dead World|consumed]] Sirene.{{Fn|1}}

Vaniel.wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Chief Librarian]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]], when the [[Ork]] forces of [[The Beast]] invaded the [[Imperium]]. Once [[Ullanor]], was determined to be where The Beast's forces originated from, Vaniel joined as part of the strike force sent to invade the world, in order to kill the Warboss. However, when the strike force arrived at Ullanor they were unable to use their ships to discover the Warboss' location, due to the world being enveloped in [[psychic]] energy. With time running short, [[Chapter Master]] [[Koorland]], asked for the [[Space Marine]] [[Chapter]]s present to gather their Librarians together; in order for them to combine their powers, so they could pierce Ullanor's physic veil. Vaniel was charged with focusing the Librarians' power for the ritual and they entered into a connected trance, where they were able to discover that The Beast was present in an Ork city known as '''Gorkogrod'''. However disaster struck before they were able to learn the exact location of the city, when the Chief Librarian was overwhelmed by the Orks' physic energy. As Vaniel served as a conduit for the ritual, the Ork's energy soon spread to the rest of the Librarians present and nearly overwhelmed all of them. Only the [[Rune Priest]] [[Thorild]] was able to initially resist the Ork's physic power and he was able to help most of the others resist before he broke the trance they were in. As soon as he did so though, Vaniel and two other Librarians, who had fallen under the Ork's power, began attacking those around them. The maddened Chief Librarian was able to kill the Librarians [[Redolphio]] and [[Carrigan Nos]] before he was killed by the Rune Priest Thorild; which severed the ritual's connection to the Ork's physic energy and ended its influence on the Librarians.{{Fn|1}}

Var Jahan.wikitext:
{{NightLordsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Night Lords]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}} 

An old veteran born on [[Terra]], he fought in the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] before the rediscovery of [[Konrad Curze]] and thus was more of a tactician than a murderer.{{Fn|1b}} Eventually rising to commander of the [[27th Company (Night Lords)|27th Company]], Var Jahan was one of only three surviving [[Kyroptera]] Captains after the disastrous [[Dark Angels]] ambush during the [[Thramas Crusade]]. During the arguments over what should be done following Curze's wounding at the hands of [[Lion El'Jonson]], [[First Captain]] [[Jago Sevatarion]] and his [[Atramentar]] killed fellow Captains [[Malithos Kuln]] and [[Cel Herec]]. Var Jahan was spared, for he was smart enough to know something was amiss before Sevatar's purge had begun.{{Fn|1a}} Later, Jahan led the forces from the ''[[Excoriator (Ship)|Excoriator]]'' when Curze ordered the Dark Angels' flagship ''[[Invincible Reason]]'' to be boarded. Var Jahan was either killed or captured by the Dark Angels during the ensuing battle.{{Fn|1c}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}'''{{fn|2}} was a member of the [[Knights-Errant]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|2}}

===History===
He was a former [[Librarian]] of the [[Blood Angels]] and detested his Primarch, [[Sanguinius]], though it was not explained why.{{Fn|1}} Ison kept his Legion's origin a secret, finding amusement in irritating [[Macer Varren]] by refusing to answer which he originated from{{Fn|3c}}, though he had a ruby set on gold pinions as a keepsake of his abandoned legion.{{Fn|3b}}. 

Ison recruited [[Fyodor Stromgren]] to the Knights-Errant after he had been mutilated by the Night Lords{{Fn|1}}, was dispatched to recover [[Nathaniel Garro]] and detain [[Euphrati Keeler]]{{Fn|2}} and fought alongside Varren, [[Nathaniel Garro]], [[Tylos Rubio]], and [[Helig Gallor]] against [[Chaos Cultist]]s on [[Terra]].{{Fn|3d}}

After the battle against the [[Lord of the Flies]] and his minions, Ison was among those chosen by Malcador to join his [[Grey Knights|new order]]. Ison took on the title '''Satre''', who would go on to become one of the original founding Grand Masters of the [[Grey Knights]].{{Fn|3b}}

===Wargear===
As a Knight-Errant Ison's wargear included [[Mk VI|Mk VI armour]] bearing the mark of the Sigilite, a [[psychic hood]] and a [[bolt pistol]] that was described as the sole object he carries that has a splash of colour on it.{{Fn|2}} He was able to manifest red coloured psychic lightning.{{Fn|3d}}

*[[Wikipedia:Satre (Etruscan god)|Satre]] was an Etruscan God associated with [[Wikipedia:Saturn (mythology)|Saturn]] in Roman culture and [[Wikipedia:Cronus|Kronos]] in Greek culture.

'''Varnan Dreir''' is a [[Lord Marshal]] in the [[Death Korps of Krieg]] [[Regiments]].{{Fn|1}}

===History===
Varnan Dreir began his career as a lowly trooper in the [[Krieg 143rd Infantry Regiment]]. As a [[Ridemaster]] in the Regiment's [[Death Rider]]s he first rode his faithful steed '''ES819'''.{{Fn|3}} 

Dreir rose through the ranks of the [[Astra Militarum]] to eventually become a [[Lord Marshal]]. He has commanded Imperial Guard battle groups in dozens of war zones, demonstrated an uncompromising determination to achieve victory regardless of the human cost in each. Despite this outlook, he is not accused of being wasteful or irresponsible with his men. Rather, Dreir is held in great esteem but the greatest Imperial strategists and well liked by those under his command. This is due to not only his string of victories, but also willingness to personally risk his own safety by commanding and motivating from the front.{{Fn|2}}

Dreir's steed, '''ES819''', has fallen in battle multiple times and suffered wounds that in normal circumstances would have resulted in termination.  Yet on each occasion, the creature appears at the Lord Marshals side once again fully recovered and repaired. Some Krieg soldiers claim the two are unkillable due to having been blessed by the [[Emperor]] Himself. Dreir holds no such belief, and knows one day his time will come.{{Fn|2}}

[[Chaplain]] '''Varnus''' was a member of the [[Adeptus Astartes]] and belonged to the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]].

== Biography==
[[Image:Chaplain_Varnus.jpg|thumb|right|Chaplain Varnus of the [[Ultramarines]].]]
Varnus was the leader of a detachment of Ultramarines Space Marines that were sent to the planet [[Lorn V]] where he was the leader of a bodyguard unit tasked with the protection as well as delivery of a [[Titan]]'s [[Princeps]] and crew to the site of the abandoned machine [[Dominatus]].

Whilst engaging in his mission, his [[Thunderhawk]] gunship was shot down by [[Chaos Space Marines]]. Only Varnus and a handful of his troops survived who held off waves of [[Chaos]] hordes as well as sent a distress signal that was received by [[General]] [[Sturnn]] of the [[Imperial Guard]]. These reinforcements managed to conduct a search and rescue mission behind enemy lines that succeeded in saving Varnus.

One of the noted accomplishments of Chaplain Varnus was his single handedly slaying a [[Bloodthirster]] [[Daemon]] in combat.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Dark Angels]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]], serving as the [[Equerry|adjutant]] to [[Zahariel]].{{Fn|1}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Vassago.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Vassago{{Fn|3}}]]
During the Heresy, Vassago was part of the force under [[Luther]] exiled to [[Caliban]] by [[Lion El'Jonson]]. During the political in-fighting between [[The Fallen]] on Caliban, Vassago aided his commander against those loyal to [[Lord Cypher]].{{Fn|1}}

Vassago was later part of the forces requisitioned by [[Corswain]] at [[Zaramund]] as he sought to reach [[Terra]]. Hiding his true allegiance, Vassago and his brothers took part in the [[Siege of Terra]] when Corswain attacked the [[Forbidden Fortress|Hollow Mountain]]. During the fight, he saved Corswain from the [[Daemon]] [[Vassukella]].{{Fn|2a}} After securing the Hollow Mountain, Vassago was confronted by a group of other secret [[Fallen]] who expressed their interest in using the powers of the [[Warp]] for their own ends. However Vassago refused to take part in the plan, stating that the powers of Chaos would corrupt the Dark Angels as they have all others. The other Fallen under [[Zahariel]] turned on Vassago, killing him.{{Fn|2b}}

Vellian Tersus.wikitext:
'''Vellian Tersus''' was the [[Terran]] [[Space Marine Captain|Seventh Captain]] of the [[Dusk Raiders]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] and later the [[Death Guard]] entitling him to the honorific title "[[Battle-Captain]]" during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
He was among the forces that the [[Death Guard]]'s newly rediscovered [[Primarch]] [[Mortarion]], led against [[The Order (Galaspar Cluster)|The Order]] during the [[Conquest of Galaspar]]. This battle saw them invade [[Galaspar]]'s primary [[Hive]] '''Protarkos''', where the Order's Lord Comptroller [[Avald Stevang]], ruled from.{{Fn|1a}} While the invasion initially went well, the Order's forces held the Death Guard off long enough for Galaspar's other Hives to come to its aid. As their armies reached Protarkos, Mortarion knew the Death Guard would fail, unless they had more time to capture Stevang. Unfortunately the Lord Comptroller and other members of the Hive's Order personnel had hidden themselves deep within one of the Hive's [[Hive Spire|Spire]]s. The only way to reach them was by blasting a hole in the Spire's roof, which would require the Death Guard to climb up its surface first. However with Order's armies about to attack Protarkos, the Primarch chose to lead the Death Guard against them and charged Tersus and his squadron with capturing Stevang.{{Fn|1b}} 

The [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] and his squadron then began to climb the [[Hive Spire]], as the battle between the [[Death Guard]] and [[The Order (Galaspar Cluster)|The Order]] began outside of [[Hive]] ''Protarkos'''. As they reached the top of the Spire, though, Lord Comptroller [[Avald Stevang|Stevang]] and the rest of Protarkos' Order, became paranoid when it was not being attacked by the Death Guard. This led them to look at vidscreens attached to turrets adorning its top and they soon spotted Tersus and his squad climbing the Spire. Realizing at once what the squadron intended to do, Stevang had the Spire's turrets fire upon Tersus' forces. The Captain could do nothing for his squadron, but urge them on even as they began to be killed. He never doubted they would be successful, however, as even if Tersus was struck down, he knew his squadron would complete their mission. Moments later the Captain was killed by the Spire's weaponry, but his two surviving squadron members [[Garro]] and [[Deros]] were able to capture Stevang. They then forced the Lord Comptroller to cease firing [[Galaspar]]'s weaponry, that was keeping the Death Guard's fleet from the world.{{Fn|1c}} With this done, the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s might could be brought against Galaspar and the Order's armies were destroyed by the Death Guard's warships.{{Fn|1d}}

Venakhar.wikitext:
{{SlaaneshPortal}}{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''Venakhar''' is the [[Chaos Space Marine Apothecary]] of the [[Emperor's Children]]'s [[Perfecti]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] and serves as the second in command of its [[Chaos Lord|Knight-Commander]], [[Marduk Tamaris]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
A [[Horus Heresy]] veteran, Venakhar creates all of the [[combat stimm]]s that the [[Perfecti]] use. However the [[Chaos Apothecary]] uses still living flesh to create his concoctions, so Venakhar cripples his foes in battle so that he can later harvest their bodies. In [[M42]], Venakhar and the Perfecti had nearly defeated a [[World Eaters]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]], when the [[Emperor's Children]]'s forces were summoned to the side of their [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]]. This message was delivered to the Warband by the [[Sorcerer Lord]] [[Mauvais]], who suddenly appeared and killed the World Eaters [[Chaos Lord|Warlord]] in order to save [[Marduk Tamaris|Tamaris]]'s life. Mauvais left shortly after delivering his message to attend Fulgrim's summons, leaving a humiliated Tamaris in his wake. However, Venakhar reminded the [[Chaos Lord|Knight-Commander]] of the opportunity the summons represented and that only the weak dwelled on the past. Tamaris agreed with this and vowed to look towards the perfection the future held for him.{{Fn|1a}} 

Venakhar subsequently took part in the invasion of the Imperial world of [[Crucible (World)|Crucible]] along with the rest of his warband.{{Fn|1b}} After Fulgrim declares whoever retrieves the head of the [[Black Templars]] [[Emperor's Children]] on the world, Venakhar hopes to secure his Primarch's favor by killing [[Johannes Berengar]] instead of Tamaris. To that end, he attempts to arrange for Tamaris' death.{{Fn|1c}} However in the end, the traitorous Apothecary is killed by Tamaris.{{Fn|1d}}

Verngar.wikitext:
{{RedCorsairsPortal}}
'''Verngar the Apostate''' was a [[Space Marine]] of the [[Angels Encarmine]], until he was exiled for insisting that the [[Chapter]]'s [[Red Thirst]] was truly the touch of [[Chaos]]. 

==History==
He then turned his back on the [[Imperium]] and joined the [[Red Corsairs]], where he rose to become a high ranking officer in the [[Chaos Warband|Warband]]. Huron Blackheart considers Verngar to be a potential threat to his power and capable of becoming a powerful Chaos Lord in his own right. Verngar assumed command of the Red Corsairs who garrisoned the [[Blackstone Fortress]] which had been gifted to the renegades by  [[Ezekyle Abaddon]]. In this position while working with [[Kairos Fateweaver]], Verngar oversaw the temporary captivity of [[Primarch]] [[Roboute Guilliman]], without the knowledge or consent of Huron himself{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}.

After Guilliman's escape, Verngar returned to [[New Badab]] with the captured ''[[Macragge's Honour]]''. Huron was highly suspicious of the action, worrying Verngar may try to supplant him but criticized him for allowing Guilliman to get away. Soonafter Verngar left with the ''Macragge's Honour'' to try and discover the [[Ebon Talon]], but Huron soon pursued him in his own [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Spectre of Ruin]]''{{Fn|1}}

In the end, Blackheart agreed to allow Verngar to search for the relic, but stated he would be going along as well. By doing so, Blackheart sought to claim the Ebon Talon first and put an end to Verngar's threat to his command of the Red Corsairs{{Fn|1}}. When they reached [[Kyren]], their two forces fought together against the mutated tribes{{Fn|1c}}, but it would be Verngar who claimed the Ebon Talon first. He then made his escape with the relic, but the Talon is what made Kyren's existence possible. Its removal caused the world to begin to come apart{{Fn|1d}} and the Red Corsairs escaped before Kyren exploded{{Fn|1e}}. Afterwards, Verngar's standing within the Red Corsairs grew considerably due to recovering the relic and he now sought to further his plans of taking control of the Warband. With a group of his followers behind him, Verngar confronted Blackheart and demanded to be given command of a large fleet, so he could join the Warband's [[War for Chogoris|invasion]] of [[Chogoris]]. Blackheart refused, though, stating that despite Verngar's success, he had never taken command of a war zone that stretched over an entire [[System]]. Even some of Verngar's followers agreed with this and Huron compromised by giving him another target - the [[Invaders]]' former [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|Homeworld]] [[Ogrys]]. It was being rebuilt for the [[Chapter]] by the Imperium and the Red Corsairs' attack upon the world, would be an opportunity for Verngar to gain command experience. Blackheart would also join Verngar aboard his warship, the captured ''[[Macragge's Honour]]'', to personally oversee his leadership abilities.{{Fn|1f}} 

If Verngar was successful and impressed Blackheart, then he would be allowed to join the invasion of [[Chogoris]] with the fleet he had demanded. Verngar agreed{{Fn|1f}} and the Red Corsairs' attack on [[Ogrys]] initially went well, until the [[Red Wolves (Warband)|Red Wolves]] began disobeying [[Verngar]]'s orders. This enraged, the Red Corsair and [[Huron Blackheart|Blackheart]] was surprised, when Verngar ordered the [[Warpsmith]] [[Turazan]] to bring the Ebon Talon to him. Blackheart had been sure that Verngar could not access the relic's power and that was why he had not returned to activate the [[Chaos Warband|Warband]]'s [[Blackstone Fortress]]{{Fn|1g}}. But thanks to the aid of Turazan and the [[Sorcerer]] [[Garlon Souleater]]{{Fn|1f}}, Verngar was able to wield the Ebon Talon's destructive fiery might. The angered Red Corsair was then about to unleash this upon the Red Wolves' ''[[Wolf of Fenris]]'' warship, had Blackheart not intervened due to their valued worth to the Warband. However Verngar refused to relent and Blackheart could sense that the Ebon Talon was strongly influencing Verngar to give into his anger. As they continued to argue, the Wolf of Fenris suddenly attacked ''[[Macragge's Honour]]'', as the Red Wolves would not sit ideally by and die without a fight. This distracted Verngar and Blackheart struck his attempted usurper with the [[Tyrant's Claw]]'s flames, in order to finally end Verngar's threat to his leadership. Verngar quickly recovered, though, and then aimed the Ebon Talon at Blackheart. However his connection to the [[Hamadrya]], allowed Blackheart to easily [[psychically]] deflect the relic's power onto Turazan. As the Warpsmith burned alive, Blackheart ended the fight by seriously wounding Verngar and then lopping off his hand that held the Ebon Talon{{Fn|1g}}.

'''Vespasian''' was a [[Lord Commander]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. The Emperor's Children were assigned to the [[28th Expedition Fleet]].

===History===
Described as having classical features, Vespasian was one of the greatest warriors of the Emperor's children. Vespasian was noted by First Captain [[Julius Kaesoron]] as being controlled, graceful and utterly deadly. Warriors who followed Vespasian would take their lead from him in all things. As a role model he set an example of how best to achieve perfection through purity of purpose. Vespasian's strong moral values stood in stark contrast to his less virtuous counterpart, another Lord Commander of the III Legion, [[Eidolon (Emperor's Children)|Eidolon]].

Vespasian led the operations on Twenty-Eight Three, a planet also known as [[Laer]] during the campaign that would later be referred to as the [[Cleansing of Laeran]]. Unknown to the Emperor's Children, the Laer were worshippers of [[Chaos]]. After the Cleansing of Laeran, the corruption of Chaos began to spread throughout the Emperor's Children. Vespasian, staunchly adhering to his ethos, resisted the arrogance and hubris commonly found now in the legion. Ignorant to the existance of Chaos; over the course of weeks or months Vespasian consulted  other like minded members of the legion, including the Second Company's captain [[Solomon Demeter]], about his growing concerns.

Vespasian was present on [[Tarsus]], an Eldar [[Maiden Worlds|maiden world]], during a meeting with [[Eldrad Ulthran]] — Farseer of the [[Ulthwé]] Craftworld. During this conference, the Eldar warned [[Fulgrim]] and his delegation of Horus' fall to Chaos and of the future rebellion. Fulgrim utterly rejected the accusations of the Eldar and a battle concluded the meeting. Vespasian reluctantly destroyed Tarsus and the rest of the maiden worlds the expedition had recently encountered with [[virus bombs]] after being ordered by Fulgrim. Weeks later, the 28th Expedition rendezvoused with Horus' [[63rd Expedition]] as ordered by the Council of Terra. Fulgrim had been ordered to inquire into reports the Council had received about the conduct of the 63rd Expedition and information of the Warmaster's grievous injuries suffered on a moon of [[Davin]]. Vespasian was not included in the delegation that met with Horus further underlining the growing rift between Vespasian and his Primarch.

Vespasian met his end after an operation conducted by the III Legion to cleanse Deep Orbital Station DS109 in the [[Callinedes]] system of an Ork infestation. Having been unusually denied a meeting with Fulgrim after numerous requests, Vespasian felt obliged to act after he observed Solomon Demeter's 2nd Company intentionally abandoned. Seizing the moment, Vespasian confronted Fulgrim in his staterooms over the growing rot and decay of the ideals that their Legion was founded on. To his horror Vespasian discovered too late the influence Chaos held over his Primarch. It was then that Fulgrim murdered Vespasian by stabbing him in the neck with [[Anathame]].{{Fn|1}}

Vextrum and [[Thane (House Cawdor)|Thane]] [[Hester (House Cawdor)|Hester]], became revered by [[House Cawdor]] due to their refinement of the [[Holy Book of Brayne]], which effectively changed the structures of the House. Vezuel.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Epistolary]] in the [[Dark Angels]] [[Chapter]] who is fighting in the war-enveloped [[Traxis Sector]]. Later in that conflict, he was given a command of a strike force from his Chapter and charged with defending the [[Death World]] [[Nectavus VI]]; after it was invaded by the [[Fallen Angel]]{{Fn|1a}} [[Sorcerer]] [[Sathariel|Sathariel the Innvokator]].{{Fn|1c}} The strike force is not along in this task however, as the [[Vostroyan Firstborn]] [[Regiment]] of [[Imperial Guard Captain|Armour Captain]] [[Grigory Maksim]] has been sent to aid them in saving the Death World; though the Vostroyan, do not know of the ties Sathariel has to the Dark Angels.{{Fn|1b}}

After both forces arrived on Nectavus VI they began fighting their way through its jungles, to reach Sathariel;{{Fn|1b}} but the Sorcerer had already begun a [[Chaos]] ritual,{{Fn|1c}} which soon opened a [[Warp]] portal in the Death World's orbit. Sathariel planned to turn Nectavus Vi into a [[Daemon World]], through which the forces of Chaos would have a permanent foothold into the Traxis Sector, and as soon as the Warp portal opened, it not only began corrupting the Death World, but also unleashed a tide of [[Daemons]] upon its surface.{{Fn|1d}} Now Grigory and Vezuel's forces are racing against time, to kill Sathariel before his ritual is completed;{{Fn|1b}} as the Sorcerer's death would force the Warp portal to close and save Nectavus VI from damnation.{{Fn|1d}}

Vhakis.wikitext:
{{IronWarriorsPortal}}
'''Ancient {{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] in the [[Iron Warriors]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]].{{Fn|1}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Vhakis.jpeg|thumb|right|220px|Ancient {{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
He was the born heir to one of the many warlords on [[Olympia]] that were forced to kneel to the [[Primarch]] [[Perturabo]] before he was reunited with the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]]. When Perturabo finally joined the [[Great Crusade]], Vhakis was judged worthy of joining the Iron Warriors and served faithfully for seventy years until he was struck down while leading the final assault on the '''Aethereal Bastion'''. However, despite his injuries, Vhakis still clung to life and, due to his stoic devotion to duty and his unquestioning loyalty to his Primarch, he earned the right to be interred within a Contemptor Dreadnought.{{Fn|1}}

After his internment, Vhakis continued to faithfully serve the Iron Warriors and when the [[Horus Heresy]] began, he joined his Legion in turning against the [[Imperium]]. He would go on to take part in the [[Dropsite Massacre]] and afterwards was one of the many Iron Warriors that were left behind to hunt down any surviving [[Loyalist]]s while the rest of his Legion took to the stars to battle the forces of the Emperor. Vhakis later met his end, however, when he was among a dozen of the Iron Warriors' Dreadnoughts that were destroyed in an ambush launched by the remnants of the [[Raven Guard]] Legion, deep within the '''Illium Rifts'''.{{Fn|1}}

Vheren Ashurhaddon{{Fn|4b}} |}} {{Character |Portal ={{SonsOfHorusPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =AshurArt.jpg |Caption ={{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|4e}} |Title =The First [[Reaver Attack Squad|Reaver]] |Homeworld =[[Cthonia]] |Birth =c. [[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - ??? |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Horus]]
("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *Captain of the [[Sons of Horus]] 23rd [[Chapter]] *Leader of the [[True Sons of Cthonia]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Former) **[[Sons of Horus]] ***[[Reaver Attack Squad]] ***23rd Chapter ***[[True Sons of Cthonia]] *[[Dark Empire]] |Notes = }} '''Vheren Ashurhaddon, the First Reaver''' was a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] in the [[Sons of Horus]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Great Crusade]], [[Horus Heresy]],{{Fn|4b}} and [[Great Scouring]].{{Fn|4c}} He was best remembered for his role in the [[Siege of Cthonia]], when he attempted to stem the Sons of Horus' [[Chaos|corruption]] and ruination by retaking their [[Homeworld]].{{Fn|4a}}{{Fn|4b}} ===History=== Ashurhaddon was born in the underground tunnels of [[Cthonia]], and was recruited into the [[Luna Wolves]] soon after [[Primarch]] [[Horus]] was united with his [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]].{{Fn|4d}} A skilled commander, he rose to [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[23rd Chapter (Sons of Horus)|23rd Chapter]] of the Luna Wolves (later Sons of Horus). Over the course of the Great Crusade, he gathered great renown and was firmly loyal to his Primarch, although he never became a member of the Legion's inner circle.{{Fn|4a}} Ashurhaddon quickly developed a disdain for the [[Terra]]n members of his Legion, seeing the ways of Cthonia as superior to any other way of warfare. Accordingly, he surrounded himself with Cthonians and devoted himself to honing the Cthonian traditions of gang warfare into strategies and tactics; for instance, he pioneered what later became known as the [[Reaver Attack Squad]], earning the nickname "The First Reaver".{{Fn|4d}} He followed Horus into treason, serving with distinction in the Horus Heresy. However, as the civil war developed, Ashurhaddon gradually realized the decline of the Sons of Horus under the corrupting influence of Chaos. This affirmed his view that the Legion had to remain devoted to the old ways of Cthonia, choosing honor over the increasingly senseless and brutal ways of war resulting from the Chaotic influences. Ashurhaddon gathered like-minded Space Marines around him, eventually rising to lead a warrior society called the "[[True Sons of Cthonia]]".{{Fn|4a}} By the end of the [[Solar War]], the calls for the internal reform of the Legion by Ashurhaddon and his followers were largely ignored by Horus and his inner circle.{{Fn|4a}} Despite becoming disgusted at what he perceived as the Legion's ruin, he could also not bring himself to actually opposing his Primarch.{{Fn|4d}} However, Horus eventually allowed the Ashurhaddon's traditionalists to attempt to retake their [[Homeworld]] Cthonia, which had been [[First Siege of Cthonia|conquered]] by the [[Imperial Fists]] during the early Heresy. Ashurhaddon thus gathered his True Sons, by then numbering over 20,000 Space Marines, and numerous supportive groups belonging to Traitor [[Imperial Army]] units and the [[Dark Mechanicum]]. He was also joined by more enigmatic groups such as a strong [[Word Bearers]] force led by [[Zedak Mordakar]] and an [[Alpha Legion]] unit, perhaps naively believing his force stronger with instead of without these additional Marines. Ultimately, the Captain hoped that he could restore the honor and old ways by reuniting the Sons of Horus with their homeworld.{{Fn|4a}} Thus, in 013.[[M31]], as the rest of the Sons of Horus invaded the [[Imperium]]'s [[Throneworld]] in the [[Siege of Terra]], Ashurhaddon led his True Sons to [[Second Siege of Cthonia|free]] Cthonia from the Imperium's grasp. Ashurhaddon's initial attack succeeded in doing so, even as the Siege of Terra raged, and he destroyed the Imperium's orbital defenses around his Homeworld. With his fleet now dominant above the world, the Captain launched a counter-invasion that began to overwhelm the Imperial forces stationed on Cthonia.{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|4a}}{{Fn|4b}} Ashurhaddon developed a bitter rivalry with [[Evander Garrius]], and the two nearly fought to the death over Horus' personal throne in the final stages of the battle at the Traitor's Gate. However while badly wounded, Ashurhaddon was evacuated by his Chieftain captain [[Ithan Ryaeve]] shortly before Cthonia was destroyed.{{Fn|4c}} ===Wargear=== Ashurhaddon wielded a [[power axe]] known as the ''[[Axe Serpentis]]'' and a pair of modified [[bolt pistol]]s known as the ''[[Banestrike Fusilade]]''. In battle, he wore the [[Panoply of the Void]].{{Fn|3}}{{Fn|4d}} ===Images=== [[Image:AshurhaddonMini.jpg|thumb|center|250px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|3}}]] ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *Ashurhaddon was an Assyrian King famous for conquering Egypt in the 600s B.C. ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2023/03/23/decide-the-fate-of-cthonia-with-the-first-horus-heresy-campaign-book/ Warhammer Community: Decide the Fate of Cthonia With the First Horus Heresy Campaign Book (Posted on 22/03/2023)] (Last accessed on 22/03/2023) *{{Endn|2}}: [[Traitor's Faith (Short Story)]] — [[Cthonia's Reckoning (Anthology)]] *{{Endn|3}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2023/04/30/the-commanders-of-the-siege-of-cthonia-work-out-their-bitter-rivalry-in-warhammer-the-horus-heresy/ Warhammer Community: The Commanders of the Siege of Cthonia Work Out Their Bitter Rivalry in Warhammer: The Horus Heresy (posted 30/4/2023)] (last accessed 30/4/2023) *4: [[Campaigns of the Age of Darkness: The Siege of Cthonia]]: **{{Endn|4a}}: pgs. 34-43 — ''The Beginning of the End'' **{{Endn|4b}}: pgs. 44-57 — ''A Bitter Homecoming'' **{{Endn|4c}}: pgs. 98-103 — ''Dead Worlds and Broken Dreams'' **{{Endn|4d}}: pgs. 212-213 **{{Endn|4e}}: pg. 63 {{DEFAULTSORT:Ashurhaddon, Vheren}} [[Category:Characters (Born: Cthonia)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Sons of Horus)]] [[fr:Vheren Ashurhaddon]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Archon]] of the [[Kabal of the Flayed Mask]]{{Fn|1a}}, until a plot to resurrect the long dead [[Archon]] [[El'uriaq]] led to a [[Dysjunction]] striking [[Commorragh]].{{Fn|1b}}

In the resulting mayhem, the Flayed Mask and its neighbor, the [[Kabal of the Twisted Sword]], were attacked by their many enemies, as well as rampaging [[Daemon]]s.  Despite their numerous foes, however, the Flayed Mask and Twisted Sword were set to emerge victorious, until the coming of the [[Black Heart Kabal]], led by Archon [[Valossian Sythrac]].{{Fn|1c}}  Sythrac was charged by Commorragh's ruler, [[Asdrubael Vect]], to restore order to the Dark City and was given free reign to attack any Kabals that refused to put down their arms and re-pledge their loyalty to Vect.{{Fn|1b}}  When the Archon's forces neared their location though, the Kabals and their enemies were so engaged in their battle that they did not immediately recognize the Black Hearts and fired upon them, killing several of Sythrac's troops.  This sealed the Kabals fate{{Fn|1c}} and both they and their enemies were destroyed by the Black Hearts.  As his Kabal was brought to ruin around him, Vhigis attempted to escape, but was hunted down and killed by Sythrac.  Now his soul is trapped within Sythrac's armour, along with the Black Heart Archon's many other victims.{{Fn|1a}}

Vianco Locard.wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
'''Vianco Locard''' is a [[Genetor]] of the [[Magos Biologis]] who specializes in the study of [[Tyranids]].

His [[bionic]] implants included caliper-shaped legs, metallic hands, and an augmetic eye{{Fn|1a}}.

== History ==
{{spoiler|source=Ultramarines (Novel Series)}}
=== Tarsis Ultra ===
{{main|Battle of Tarsis Ultra}}
Locard accompanied [[Inquisitor Lord]] [[Kryptman]] to [[Tarsis Ultra]] in late 999 [[M41]], to assist in the defense against a tendril of [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]]{{Fn|1a}}. As the battle progressed, he dissected and examined the corpses of enemy creatures, seeking a pure genetic strain that would allow him to develop a poison that could do maximum damage to the Hive Fleet{{Fn|1b}}.

His efforts were frustrated by the rapid mutation of the Tyranid specimens, until a [[Deathwatch]] team assigned to Kryptman managed to capture a [[Lictor]] that had infiltrated the capital city well ahead of the main invasion{{Fn|1c}}.

Using the Lictor's relatively unchanged gene sequence, Locard developed a poison that overstimulated the creature's adaptive processes, triggering a frenzy of evolutionary changes that caused too much strain for its body to survive{{Fn|1d}}. With this poison, the Deathwatch team, led by [[Uriel Ventris]], boarded the splinter fleet's last remaining [[Hive Ship]] and infected the [[Norn Queen]], causing a chain reaction that caused the remaining Tyranids on the planet to die{{Fn|1e}}.

=== The Heraclitus Effect ===
The Imperial forces' triumph was short-lived. A short time after the Tyranid invasion, [[Warsmith]] [[Honsou]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] seized control of one of Tarsis Ultra's orbital space stations and used it to launch torpedoes that devastated the planet's cities, and introduced an agricultural virus which caused the remaining Tyranid bio-forms to grow at an exponential rate, eventually consuming the entire planet.

After Honsou and his forces departed, Locard investigated the scene of the attack, and swore retribution against whoever was responsible for it{{Fn|2}}.

Locard also recovered a helmet, from the suit of [[power armour]] that Uriel Ventris had left behind on [[Medrengard]], that Honsou had fired onto the planet's surface, making the connection between his attack and his vendetta against Uriel{{Fn|3b}}.

=== Ultramar ===
Given his past history with the Ultramarines, and his interest in the fate of Tarsis Ultra, Locard led a team of Adepts and Mechanicus soldiery to [[Ultramar]], to assist the Ultramarines with defending against Honsou's army, the [[Bloodborn]]{{Fn|3a}}.

This team accompanied Uriel and the Ultramarines' Fourth Company to [[Calth]], where he made several important contributions: tapping into Uriel's latent memories to discover his link with [[The Newborn]]{{Fn|3d}}; and developing countermeasures to the [[scrapcode]] attacks of Honsou's [[Dark Mechanicus]] adept, [[Cycerin]], which the Iron Warriors were using to bypass or sabotage Ultramar's defenses{{Fn|3e}}{{Fn|3f}}.

He also deployed a large force of [[Skitarii]] and [[Praetorian]]s to assist the Ultramarines and Calth [[PDF]] in fighting off Honsou's troops{{Fn|3c}}.

At the conclusion of the campaign, he was one of the few non-Ultramarines allowed to attend the formal victory ceremony in the [[Temple of Correction]] on [[Macragge]]{{Fn|3g}}.

Though he was derided by Dalanthe's adult citizens who did not believe the children's stories, the Freeblade stood watch for three long months, until a [[Daemonic]] [[Lord of Skulls]] finally breached the [[Warp]] and appeared on the Agri World. It soon began rampaging through Dalanthe's population, until {{PAGENAME}} stood in its way and, though his suit was torn apart by the [[Lord of Skulls]], the Freeblade was able to decapitate the [[Daemon Engine]] as his last act. His sacrifice banished the Gorehaunter back to the Warp for a thousand years{{Fn|1}} and {{PAGENAME}} has become famously known, even millennia later, for slaying the Lord of Skulls.{{Fn|2}}

Viktor Hark.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Viktor Hark''' was a [[Commissar]]{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|2a}} who served on [[Lord General]] [[Lugo|Lugo's]] [[General Staff|staff]] during the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1d}} He was attached to the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]] of the [[Astra Militarum]] for their seemingly final mission on [[Hagia]]{{Fn|1a}}, and remained with them following their unexpected success on that world.{{Fn|1f}}{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2b}}


==Biography==
===Hagia===
For some time, the [[General Staff]] of the Sabbat Crusade had been considering appointing a Commissar to the [[Tanith First and Only]]; the regiment's commanding officer, [[Ibram Gaunt]], held the unusual rank of [[Colonel-Commissar]], bestowed on him by [[Warmaster]] [[Slaydo]], and many in Crusade command believed that Gaunt was not capable of handling the conflicting duties of a [[Colonel]] and [[Commissar]]. This concern was brought to the forefront in the [[Hagia]] campaign.{{Fn|1a}}

The reconquest of Hagia, which had been subjugated by [[Pater (Chaos)|Pater]] [[Sin]] and his [[Infardi]], was a morally important theatre of the Crusade, as Hagia was both the birth- and burial place of [[Saint Sabbat]] herself. Gaunt had command of the Imperial forces committed to the recapture of [[Holy Doctrinopolis|Hagia's capital]] but [[Lord General]] [[Lugo]], impatient and eager for victory, pressured Gaunt into taking the city quickly, not caring for collateral damage or caution in the face of [[Chaos|the Archenemy]]. Lugo ordered Gaunt to abandon his infantry-based approach in favour of an armoured assault by the [[Eighth Pardus Armoured]], which led to Imperial forces triggering a [[psychic]] booby trap that not only killed a large number of [[Brevian Centennials|Brevian guardsmen]], but also acted as an [[astropathic]] beacon summoning Chaos reinforcements to Hagia.{{Fn|1a}}

Lugo was left no choice but to order the evacuation of Hagia, abandoning the planet to the forces of Chaos.{{Fn|1a}} Hark, however, both admired Gaunt and realised that the Lord General was trying to find a scapegoat to cover up his own failures. He suggested to Lugo that Gaunt and the Tanith First should be charged with a final mission - to travel to the [[Shrinehold of Saint Sabbat]] and retrieve the Saint's bones for transport offworld.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1d}} Hark was attached to the regiment for this operation, charged with keeping Gaunt in line and ensuring that he did not fail in this task.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

When Gaunt and his honour guard reached the Shrinehold, however, Gaunt decided not to remove the Saint's remains. Instead he chose to hold position and defend the shrine against the attacking Chaos forces - partly due to Sabbat's deathbed prophecy, which predicted disaster if her bones were ever taken from Hagia, and also because there was little chance of breaking through the Infardi army that had pursued them into the mountains. Hark protested this decision and threatened to detain or execute Gaunt, as it went against explicit orders, but backed down after some of the other officers in the honour guard threatened to shoot him.{{Fn|1d}} In the battle to defend the shrine, Hark managed to save the life of [[Major]] [[Elim Rawne|Rawne]] by taking out a [[SteG 4]] with his [[plasma pistol]].{{Fn|1e}}

===Tanith First and Only===
After the actions at Hagia Hark became the second commissar of the Tanith First, dealing more with the day to day commissariat duties while Colonel-Commissar Gaunt dealt with the command duties of running the regiment.{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|2c}}

Fighting with the Tanith through actions at [[Phantine (planet)|Phantine]], [[Herodor]] and [[Aexe Cardinal]], he became an integral part of the regiment. During the [[Battle of Herodor]] he lost part of his arm to a [[Loxatl]] [[flechette blaster]] round and had it replaced by a [[Imperial bionics|bionic]].{{Fn|3a}}

When Ibram Gaunt went on the mission to [[Gereon]] Hark was the head Commissar for the Tanith. But during the time between Gaunt's mission on Gereon and his return the Tanith First had been mixed with the [[Belladon 81st Recon Regiment]] and became the [[81st/1st Recon]]. After the campaign during "His Last Command", the Tanith First was reformed and was back under the command of Gaunt, with Hark returning to his role as the chief political commissar while Gaunt commanded the regiment.

==Wargear==
Hark is known to have used an antique [[plasma pistol]].{{Fn|1c}} He was also the only combatant in the regiment not to own a [[Tanith warknife]], instead preferring a standard-issue pugio dagger with a broad blade and a golden [[aquila]] crest.{{Fn|2c}}

Vilius.wikitext:
{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Emperor's Children]] [[Chaos Lord]] who served as a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] in the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}} 

Born on [[Chemos]], Vilius rose to become a fine commander in his [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]. Yet his fellow Legion member [[Narvo Quin]] remarked this ended, when the Emperor's Children fell into [[Slaanesh]]'s grasp and Vilius became lost to his own hedonism{{Fn|2b}}. He once made a wager with [[Zarghan Ironfist]], who was a member of his [[Space Marine Company|Company]], but Vilius did not pay his debt after he lost the wager. In retaliation, Zarghan launched a surprise raid on Vilius' palace and crucified all of the Captain's pleasure-slaves.  This latest infraction of discipline would get Zarghan expelled from the Legion, but that did nothing to abate Vilius' anger against his former comrade and the anger still remains with him even now.{{Fn|1}}

Vilius would later be among the Emperor's Children Warbands, that the [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]] sent to aid [[Fabius Bile]] in the [[Battle of Belial IV]]. The [[Chaos Lord]] was reluctant to help, but Bile quickly reminded Vilius that due to his reputation few other Traitor [[Apothecaries]] were willing to work with him. And even those Apothecaries who agreed to work with Vilius, would still be under threat from the vengeful [[Coven of the Thirteen Scars]], as Bile had taught many of them. If Vilius wanted to keep his Warband functioning, he had no choice but to fight in order to save Bile from the Coven{{Fn|2a}}. The Chaos Lords were ultimately convinced, however, to take part in the battle by [[Narvo Quin]]{{Fn|2b}}, who threatened them by claiming both [[Slaanesh]] and [[Fulgrim]] demanded they aid Bile. If they refused, the Chaos Lords would ultimately damn themselves as cowards in the eyes of their God and Primarch.{{Fn|2a}}

Voeder Lenck.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
[[Corporal]] '''Voeder Lenck''' was a non-commissioned officer of the [[Cadian Shock Troops]], and the commander of a [[Leman Russ Exterminator]] tank during [[Operation Thunderstorm]] on [[Golgotha]].

==Biography==
Aged twenty-eight at the time of Operation Thunderstorm, Lenck was handsome, dashing, and a rogue, more of a "gang boss" than a soldier, a type found all too often hiding beneath an [[Imperial Guard]] uniform.  He had acquired an evil reputation back on [[Cadia]], and continued to run his various scams and cons after joining the expedition force.

His tank crew looked up to him and counted on him to garner them extra rations and illicit goods, and help them avoid their more onerous duties, such as labor details.  Like many successful rogues, Lenck always knew exactly how to appear on his official record and in front of officers and [[commissar]]s.

During the expedition, the only soldier who failed to warm to him was [[Imperial Guard Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Oskar Wulfe]], who recognized Lenck's type, even as Lenck treated him with all respect in public, even saving his tank's life in combat with [[ork]]s, with a single well-aimed shot from his Exterminator.

Lenck was annoyed by Wulfe's obvious suspicion, and eavesdropped on Wulfe and several of his crew, eventually learning that Wulfe was suffering hallucinations of comrades he had lost on [[Palmeros]].  Lenck needled Wulfe with a veiled reference to these hallucinations, which rattled Wulfe.

After the final battle with the orks, and as the Expedition was preparing to depart Golgotha, Lenck ambushed Wulfe alone on the battlefield, while the Sergeant was saying his goodbyes to lost friends.  Lenck was faster and trickier, but Wulfe gained the upper hand by stabbing Lenck's arm with the tusk of a [[Nob]] Wulfe had killed.  Pinned, Lenck begged for his life, but Wulfe said he couldn't kill a fellow [[Cadian]], even a piece of scum like Lenck - both their lives belonged only to the [[Emperor]].  Wulfe did, however, smash Lenck's face with his elbow, permanently disfiguring his once-handsome looks.

Wulfe then dumped Lenck's unconscious form at the feet of his stunned crew, asking if any of them wished to avenge their fallen "boss."  No one did.  Instead, the crew gathered up Lenck and departed with the rest of the expedition force.

Vorx.wikitext:
{{NurglePortal}}{{DeathGuardPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Chaos Lord]] and [[Siegemaster]] of the [[Lords of Silence]] Warband.{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
[[Image:Vorx.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
Vorx was among the first [[Aspirants]] taken from [[Barbarus]] to join the [[Death Guard]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] after his [[Primarch]] [[Mortarion]] was discovered by the [[Emperor]]. He then took part in the battles of the [[Great Crusade]] and eventually rose to become a fleet commander, known as a Siegemaster, within the Legion. When the [[Horus Heresy]] began, Vorx joined his Legion in turning upon the [[Imperium]], but after [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]]' forces were defeated in the [[Battle of Terra]], he fled with the other traitors into the [[Eye of Terror]]. It was sometime later, that Vorx formed the [[Lords of Silence]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]], which has gone on to become one of the Death Guard's most powerful Warbands.{{Fn|1a}}

After the opening of the [[Great Rift]], Vorx and the Lords of Silence allied with the [[Weeping Veil]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] of the [[Word Bearers]] and attacked [[Sabatine]] — [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|homeworld]] of the [[White Consuls]] [[Space Marines Chapter]]{{Fn|1b}}. Vorx managed not only to defeat the White Consuls, and personally kill its [[Chapter Master]] [[Cymar Xydias]]{{Fn|1c}}, but he also disrupted the [[Chaos]] sacrifices, the traitorous Weeping Veil had attempted in order to claim Sabatine for themselves{{Fn|1d}}. As a result, the Word Bearer Warband was forced to leave the world and Sabatine became the fertile ground for new diseases and maladies, as the Lords of Silence began to turn it into a copy of the [[Plague Planet]]. Afterwards, Vorx remained uncertain whether to stay on the newly conquered world or respond to the call of his [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Mortarion]] and join the [[Death Guard]]'s [[Plague Wars|assault]] on [[Ultramar]].{{Fn|1e}}

He alone of his recruiting class captured a unique beast. For his mantle he slew a mottled tri-horn, amongst the most vicious and cunning of their reptilian breed. Even teams of veteran drake-hunters might struggle to accomplish such a deed. He'stan's skills as a smith – working his hammer upon the anvil – were such that the master artificers stopped over his works and admired them.{{Fn|5}} He'stan was originally the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[4th Company (Salamanders)|4th company]] and served in that role for a century. The Chapter Council then called him to set aside his duties as captain and become the Forgefather. As he let go of his old duties, he also received a new name; Vulkan He'stan. As a result, he lost his original name.{{Fn|1}} ===Forgefather=== As Forgefather, He'stan has worked his way from system to system in search of the [[Artefacts of Vulkan|nine artefacts of Vulkan]], his only clues coming from the [[Tome of Fire]], which is extremely difficult to interpret, let alone put into use. Instead of calling solely on members of the fourth company, He'stan can call on any number of Salamanders to aid him in his quest. The Salamanders are more than happy to cleanse an area of a world on a rumour that a piece of their history is there.{{Fn|1}} He'stan accompanied [[Herculon Praetor]] and the [[Firedrakes]] when they went in pursuit and rescue of [[Chaplain]] [[Elysius]], to retrieve [[Vulkan's Sigil]]. During this time they battled the [[Dark Eldar]] and had to infiltrate the [[webway]] and a Dark Eldar city, where it was revealed that the Forgefather knew the language of the enemy.{{Fn|2b}} The [[Necron]] warlord [[Trazyn the Infinite]] has attempted to obtain the [[Artifacts of Vulkan]] for himself, but He'stan defeated Trazyn in personal combat in 878.[[M41]] and again in the [[Tochran Crusade]] in 943.[[M41]].{{Fn|3}} In the wake of the [[Great Rift]]'s creation, many believe He'stan's quest is now impossible to complete. The Forgefather, however, thinks this a test by [[Vulkan]] to fully temper his sons, before the [[Primarch]] rejoins the Salamanders.{{Fn|6a}} He and a party of Salamanders later journeyed to the world of [[Zero]] alongside the [[Hammers of Nocturne]] and [[Covenant of Fire]], as He'stan believed it contained a clue to the location of the [[Unbound Flame]].{{Fn|6b}}{{Fn|7}} Once there, however, he was confronted by the [[Alpha Legion]], who had infiltrated the Covenant of Fire and swayed much of the world to their cause. Whilst Vulkan and his Salamanders eventually prevailed and forced the Alpha Legion to retreat, they could find no source of the Unbound Flame. Afterwards, he has pushed even deeper into the [[Imperium Nihilus]] in search of the missing artefacts.{{Fn|9}} ===Wargear=== He'stan carries three of the nine relics left behind by his namesake and [[Primarch]]: *The [[Spear of Vulkan]], which can burn [[ceramite]]{{Fn|1}}. He'stan often throws the Spear, enabling the strength of the weapon to be used at range.{{Fn|2a}} *[[Kesare's Mantle]], a legendary drakescale cloak, granting He'stan extra protection due to its strength.{{Fn|1}} *The [[Gauntlet of the Forge]], an armoured gauntlet that is also a heavy flamer.{{Fn|1}} ==Images== VulkanHestan.jpg|Vulkan He'stan 5th Edition Miniature VulkanHestan10th.jpg|Vulkan He'stan 10th Edition Miniature{{Fn|8}} VulkanHestanArt.jpg|'''Vulkan He'stan''' with the '''Spear of Vulkan'''{{Fn|1}} ==See also== *[[Vulkan He'stan: Forgefather (Short Story)]] ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Space Marines (5th Edition)]], pg. 93 *2: [[Firedrake (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 169 **{{Endn|2b}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 224 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Space Marines (6th Edition)]] (E-Book Edition), pgs. 194–197 *{{Endn|4}}: [http://www.blacklibrary.com/games-workshop-digital-editions/Vulkan-Hestan.html Black Library] ''(last accessed December 13 2013)'' *{{Endn|5}}: [[Warlords of the Dark Millennium: Vulkan He'stan (Background Book)]] *6: [[Codex Supplement: Salamanders (8th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|6a}}: pg. 33 - ''Legends of Nocturne: The Trials of He'stan'' **{{Endn|6b}}: pg. 36 - ''Vulkan He'stan'' *{{Endn|7}}: [[Codex: Space Marines (10th Edition)]], pg. 18 *{{Endn|8}}: [https://archive.ph/oqCtm Warhammer Community: The Big Summer Preview – Champions of the First Founding] ''(archived from [https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/meznaevz/the-big-summer-preview-champions-of-the-first-founding/ the original] 18 July 2025, last accessed 18 July 2025)'' *{{Endn|9}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/h8ovonju/vulkan-hestan-forgefather-of-the-salamanders/ Warhammer Community: Vulkan He’stan: Forgefather of the Salamanders (posted 5/8/2025)] ''(last accessed 05 August 2025)'' {{DEFAULTSORT:He'stan, Vulkan}} [[Category:Characters (Salamanders)]] [[Category:Tome of Fire (Novel Series)]] [[de:Vulkan He'stan]] [[fr:Vulkan He'stan]]
